name: IEC retriggerable monostable
summary: IEC monostable showing only the single-pulse qualifier; each new trigger restarts the output pulse.
description: The retriggerable monostable is marked with the single pulse shape without the preceding 1. Each trigger during the output pulse restarts the timing, so the output remains active as long as triggers arrive more often than the set period.

This behaviour is useful for missing-pulse detection and activity monitoring, where the output drops only when a regular signal stops. The drawing should note the expected trigger rate and the timeout chosen.

The symbol does not show whether a clear input truncates the pulse. Check for an R input and its polarity. Include reset behaviour in the timing chart so a missing-pulse indication can be distinguished from an externally forced clear.
readingNotes: Look for a clear or reset input.
drawingChecklist: Show the single-pulse qualifier without the 1.
Draw timing components and state the timeout.
distinction: The non-retriggerable form has the 1 qualifier and ignores triggers during the pulse.
